subject: Bridge strategy: hosting preference & procurement onramp
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge strategy: hosting preference & procurement onramp

Hi Emma / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and three concrete asks so we can build an accurate onboarding proposal and procurement path.

Call recap (very high level):
- Migration sources: OpenAI production endpoints + an internal legacy GPU cluster for batch scoring.
- Primary constraint: predictability for daytime traffic + need for SSO and SOC2 evidence.
- Preference expressed during call: leaning toward Dedicated capacity but open to Private VPC for regulated flows.

Three asks to unblock internal sizing and pricing:
1) QPS profile: typical daytime qps and peak QPS you expect (tokens/sec or requests/min is fine).
2) Latency SLO: target p95 for user-facing requests (we noted ~250ms earlier) and offline batch window.
3) Procurement timeline & preferred contracting model (monthly reserved / annual commit / PO & SOW).

Optional: if you can share a small sample of request telemetry (anonymized) or an example prompt distribution, that helps us recommend Dedicated pool sizes and batching strategy. If you prefer, we can provide a short telemetry collector snippet to run against a replay bucket.

I attached a short cheatsheet comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private so you can forward to legal/procurement. I looped Monica (CS) to coordinate technical onboarding and Karthik (solutions) will join for any deeper infra Qs.

Proposed next steps:
- Emma: reply with the three items above + preferred NDA/procurement path OR
- Schedule 30m follow-up next week (Mon/Tue) for sizing review and procurement alignment.

Thanks — I’ll draft an initial mutual action plan once we have those details.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-cheatsheet.pdf
From: Emma Reynolds <emma@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge strategy: hosting preference & procurement onramp

Jordan — thanks for the recap. Helpful. Answers below: feel free to forward to legal/procurement.

1) Traffic profile: typical daytime ~35 reqs/min (mostly short prompts, ~400 tokens avg). Peak spiky loads up to ~150 reqs/min for short 60s windows tied to nightly dispatch events. Batch scoring on the GPU cluster is ~5k items/day, flexible within a 6–8 hour window.

2) Latency SLO: for interactive flows we target p95 <= 300ms. For batch scoring, we care more about throughput and job completion within the window.

3) Procurement / timeline: Q3 budget approved; procurement aims to finalize by end of September. Preferred contracting: PO + SOW; open to annual commitments if price/credits justify. We will need an NDA in place before exchanging any logs or PII samples.

Security & compliance: I attached our compliance questionnaire (Acme_Compliance_Request.xlsx). We are SOC2-aligned and will require Redwood SOC2 evidence and a basic data-flow diagram for the Private VPC option.

Preference: leaning Dedicated for predictable daytime throughput, with a Private VPC option for regulated PHI flows. We're migrating most traffic from OpenAI endpoints; some internal tooling still runs on the legacy GPU cluster (on-prem).

Next step: please send NDA + a rough cost estimate for Dedicated (monthly reserved) and a delta for Private VPC. We can then set a procurement call with legal.

—Emma
Emma Reynolds
VP Product, Acme Health
emma@acmehealth.com
Attachment: Acme_Compliance_Request.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge strategy: hosting preference & procurement onramp

Emma — perfect, thanks for the detail and the questionnaire. Short replies and plan: 

- Dedicated fits the daytime predictability requirement; we’ll size a 2-4 GPU pool initially depending on peak concurrency (I’ll include a sizing sensitivity table).
- Private VPC add-on: we’ll outline networking prerequisites (VPC peering/VPN, KMS integration) and an incremental monthly run-rate.
- NDA: sending our standard mutual NDA via DocuSign link in the next message.

Action items from Redwood (what you’ll see in the MA plan):
- Sizing sensitivity (two scenarios) + estimated monthly cost for reserved capacity (1yr/30% discount estimate).
- Private VPC checklist (network, routing, certs, KMS) and SOC2 artifact list.
- Short telemetry collector snippet (Python) you can run against a small replay bucket; this is optional but will help us validate batching/latency assumptions.

Can you confirm whether the batch GPU cluster has consistent NVMe cache available (we typically recommend a temporary cache for migration jobs) and whether your legal team prefers a templated NDA or a redline?

I’ll circulate an initial estimate and the DocuSign NDA link by EOD.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge strategy: hosting preference & procurement onramp

Emma / Jordan — looping in a couple of infra/security notes from our side (short):

- SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 Type II report and a summary of control mappings. For Private VPC, we’ll provide a data-flow diagram and a runbook for tenant isolation.
- Data residency: Private VPC supports customer-managed EBS/KMS keys and regional placement — please confirm the region for PHI traffic (us-east-1 vs us-west-2).
- Migration from OpenAI: we typically provide a compatibility shim for prompt/response differences (few-line client update) and a brief eval to check rate-limit/backoff behavior.
- On-prem GPU cluster hybrid: if you’d like to keep the cluster for nightly jobs, we can set up a hybrid routing policy that sends interactive traffic to Dedicated and batch jobs to the cluster until cutover.

If you can share a short sample of request timing (anonymized) and the preferred PHI region, I’ll prepare the Private VPC prerequisites document and the network diagram.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Emma Reynolds <emma@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge strategy: hosting preference & procurement onramp

Thanks, Jordan and Karthik — this is helpful. Quick confirm:

- We will proceed with NDA before sharing any telemetry. Legal prefers a DocuSign flow (template ok).
- Region for PHI traffic: us-east-1.
- NVMe cache: the on-prem cluster has NVMe on node groups, yes — we can enable a temp cache for migration windows.
- Procurement: please send your 1yr reserved estimate and Private VPC delta. We will aim to lock by 30 Sep.

I’ve asked legal to expect the DocuSign link and procurement to expect a short MA plan and pricing sheet.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/ACME-NDA-123
Drive folder for compliance artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Once NDA is signed, we’ll push over the anonymized telemetry and schedule a 30m technical review.

—Emma

VP Product, Acme Health
